hooks.text: Tiny dwarf galaxies are missing massive amounts of expected oxygen.
Stars create oxygen, but dwarf galaxies barely hold any.
Where did all the oxygen inside nearby dwarf galaxies go?

title: Hubble Discovers Missing Oxygen in Nearby Galaxies
description: Astronomers using NASA's Hubble Space Telescope discovered that dwarf galaxies are missing massive amounts of expected oxygen. Supernova explosions trigger violent galactic winds that blast the element out into intergalactic space.

beats.text: Tiny dwarf galaxies are missing massive amounts of expected oxygen.
beats.visual: Hubble image of the NGC 6822 dwarf galaxy resolving individual stars

beats.text: Stars inside them constantly forge oxygen throughout their lives.
beats.visual: Hubble image of massive stars forming in a dwarf galaxy region

beats.text: Theoretical models predicted dwarf galaxies should keep most of it.
beats.visual: Computer simulation visual of galaxy evolution and element retention

beats.text: So Hubble analyzed 37 nearby galaxies to measure the gas.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope orbiting high above Earth in bright sunlight

beats.text: Astronomers found that these galaxies hold onto only a fraction.
beats.visual: Hubble optical view of the Leo I dwarf galaxy stars

beats.text: Supernova explosions unleash violent galactic winds across space.
beats.visual: Artist concept of energetic galactic winds driven by massive star explosions

beats.text: These massive blasts literally blow the element into intergalactic space.
beats.visual: Hubble view of supernova remnant N63A expanding into surrounding space

beats.text: They continuously strip their own stellar islands clean of oxygen.
beats.visual: Wide Hubble survey of deep space showing isolated dwarf galaxies
